All ten cited URLs returned HTTP 200 after normal redirects; architecture contracts, implementation guidance, abstract models and assurance claims remain separately scoped.

evidence: Checked host-capability, required-feature, optional-feature, admitted-set, stage-one, stage-two, permission, exit-demand, tag and generation notation.
Reviewed capability inclusion, selected acceleration, translation composition, permission intersection, reason-weighted demand and safe tag reassignment.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation separates physical support, required profile semantics, selected accelerators and guest-advertised behavior.

evidence: Executed negotiation with two required mechanisms, two optional requests and one unavailable optional accelerator.
Confirmed admission, three selected mechanisms, no missing requirement and exit-and-inject fallback; independently recomputed example exit demand as 0.59 CPU-seconds per wall-clock second.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The deterministic computation validates set negotiation only; it encodes no processor controls, dependency fields, VM entry, translation, interrupt or IOMMU behavior.

evidence: Re-derived admission from required-set inclusion and selected acceleration as required features union supported optional features.
Checked composed address translation, effective permission intersection, exit-demand summation and generation-safe tag reuse.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The relations are subsystem reasoning tools and do not claim a complete formalization of any ISA, processor, VMM, IOMMU, interrupt controller or migration system.

evidence: Reviewed reserved controls, invalid guest state, stale exit fields, stage-one versus stage-two faults, page-walk faults, tag exhaustion and incomplete invalidation.
Reviewed interrupt migration races, late DMA, reset failure, counter migration, nested-exit attribution, feature withdrawal, confidential modes and timing channels.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Capability, entry, exit, translation, invalidation, interrupt, DMA, time, nested, migration and security boundaries receive distinct treatment.

evidence: Traced capability discovery through profile construction, legal controls, VM entry, reason-specific exits, fallbacks and destination admission.
Verified privilege-domain separation, permission non-expansion, completed tag invalidation, interrupt identity, DMA ownership and declared time semantics.
invariant_checking.notes: The chapter treats CPU, translation, interrupt, I/O, time and nested state as coupled mechanisms constrained by one versioned guest contract.

evidence: Reviewed safety composition across CPU domain separation, control validation, two-stage translation, interrupt identity and I/O translation.
Constructed counterexamples for feature-bit-as-control-legality, valid-entry-as-profile-coherence, nested-paging-as-zero-walk-cost, tag-as-permanent and IOMMU-map-as-safe-passthrough.
proof_review.notes: The chapter supplies reusable hardware-assistance obligations, not a formal proof of a processor, firmware, hypervisor, device, IOMMU, platform or threat model.

evidence: Audited uses of supported, required, admitted, exposed, valid, translated, invalidated, remapped, isolated, confidential and migrated.
Confirmed architecture guarantees, capability-dependent behavior, abstract models, recommendations, examples and security limits remain separately scoped.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: A feature bit is not labeled a legal configuration, entry success is not labeled contract coherence, architectural separation is not labeled side-channel freedom and attestation is not labeled workload correctness.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/OS-082/report.json records source, expected and actual output, stderr, exit status, toolchain and environment for capability negotiation.
Reviewed required processor, stepping, microcode, firmware, kernel, VMM, CPU model, machine type, IOMMU, device, mitigation and migration-matrix evidence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The passing toy establishes one set-selection outcome only; it provides no evidence for control encoding, VM entry, nested translation, interrupt delivery, DMA containment, performance or security.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed hardware assistance as negotiated execution, translation, interrupt and I/O mechanisms whose acceleration must refine one declared virtual-machine contract.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable concerns including capability fields, entry validation, exit qualification, nested translation, tagged TLBs, interrupt posting and remapping, IOMMU teardown, virtual time, fallbacks and migration profiles. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from execution domains and control discovery through entries, exits, virtual CPUs, translations, interrupts, DMA, clocks, nesting, performance, fallback, migration and security, followed by twelve obligations, sixteen trade-offs, twenty-five misconceptions, ten examples and five complete exercises.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external operating-systems academic, ISA architect, processor or IOMMU vendor, hypervisor maintainer, security reviewer, independent-verification or certification review is claimed.
